8.  Drought State  of  Emergency  Public Works Director Igoe reported on the Drought State of Emergency per
  Governor Newsom' s Executive  Governor Newsom' s Executive Order N- 7- 22. He stated that on March 18,
  Order N- 7- 22.  2022, the Department of Water Resources ( DWR) announced it would reduce
  the State Water Project( SWP) allocation from 15 percent to 5 percent of
  requested supplies for 2022. On March 28,
  2022, Governor Gavin Newsom

  signed Executive Order N- 7- 22 proclaiming state of emergency across all the
  counties  of  California, due to extreme  and expanding drought conditions.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There were public comments. ( To hear what was said during public comment,
  archived Council meeting.)
  please visit the City' s website to view the
   City Council Minutes, Monday, April 18, 2022, Page 5,

  The City Council agreed it was necessary to implement Phase V of the City' s
  Water Conservation  Ordinance  No. 1009 and that also it will be difficult for
  residents, especially those who already put in place water conservation
  methods,  to further reduce water usage.  City Council directed staff to educate
  the residents to assist them in ways to conserve water and to reach out to
  State and Federal representatives on what they are doing to capture rainwater
  before it flows into the ocean.

  It was moved by Lau, seconded by Crosby and unanimously carried to adopt
  Resolution  No. 22- 17, to implement  Phase V of the Water Conservation,  Use
  and Restrictions Ordinance No. 1009 and to impose the California Drought
  Penalty Surcharges to gain compliance throughout the duration of the Drought
  State of Emergency.
